bug: tt-inference-server test_non_uniform_seeding: the 16 seed=0 requests of a 32-way concurrent batch are not byte-identical
root_cause: models/common/sampling/tt_sampling.py called ttnn.manual_seed BEFORE _adjust_values_for_tiebreak, so compute kernels ran on the sampling cores between the seed being installed and ttnn.sampling consuming it. ttnn.manual_seed sets a per-CORE PRNG register; an intervening kernel on that core destroys it, and the users mapped to those cores draw a different random number from the identical seed.
fix: move the ttnn.manual_seed call to immediately before ttnn.sampling (shared code, models/common/sampling/tt_sampling.py)

device_vs_host_sampling.reading: vLLM's host sampler, fed the same device logits, is uniform -> the per-row logits agree and the defect is in the device sampling path, not in numerics

serving_seed_trace.finding: every active row is handed the same absolute position and the same seed counter every step, so all 16 seed=0 rows are pushed ONE distinct device seed (e.g. 776604 at pos 73, 399475 at pos 75) at the divergence step, and one row still sampled a different token
serving_seed_trace.reading: the divergent set is exactly {0,11,22} intersected with the slots that happened to hold a seed=0 request -- a fixed set of cores, not a race

op_level_probe.setup: one device, 32 users, identical near-uniform top-32 distribution, the SAME seed pushed to all 32 users; the sampled index reveals the drawn uniform

plugin_sampling_suite.before: 6-7 failed (the documented 'seeded reproducibility at batch > 1' limitation)
